My review will be on your desk by end-of-day tomorrow.

So the art style is pretty bland. Everything looks like you are viewing the story through a sepia lens, except in color. Perhaps the point, since the entire planet is in a constant snow storm, but the aesthetic also crosses over to the characters. They don't have many features aside from the parts to make them stand out from each other (beard, black woman, white woman, overalls).

The writing really bugged me though. I read a lot of #1 books, so I am used to forced dialogue meant to give some background to the story. My issue with this particular book is that things are repeated a lot. I don't mean that one thing gets said over and over again, I mean that in one frame a character will say something and in the very next frame they will reiterate. There is a part where you might sigh and go, "We get it, this is called the New Ice Age" while simultaneously thinking "that's a long title for people to say in everyday conversation".

Although the story might not be well written, the premise is still interesting. We are introduced to some shady cargo transporters (replace Han Solo with Keaton) and they are in need of credits to purchase heat. A doctor and his daughter are trying to get from New Mexico to Alcatraz, and hope that Keaton and her gang can get them there safely. There are bounty hunters looking for this daughter doctor, as he is apparently wanted for crimes against humanity for his part in starting the New Ice Age. In an attempt to reverse global warming, they also introduced Frostbite to the planet, killing billions of people.

There is a very touching moment between a husband and wife where the husband has Frostbite and the people in the area notice it, so everyone freaks out because the government is known to destroy towns where the disease is discovered. I wont spoil the scene, but it's a powerful moment that quickly establishes the world as a place where people will do bad things out of worry.

I don't know how long I will stick with it, due to the poor dialogue, but I will definitely give it another issue to see where it goes, mostly because of the two scenes that really lingered in my mind for a bit. Hopefully they get the opportunity to let the world build naturally, and not force so much through text.
